synthesis.original_text: Would tripling trastuzumab's half-life maintain HER2 occupancy longer than improving its binding affinity tenfold?

answer.statement: Tripling half-life gives higher endpoint occupancy and occupancy AUC than tenfold stronger affinity, but both remain above the 90% threshold when the 180-day window ends, so the simulation cannot show which maintains occupancy above threshold longer; duration is censored.

missing_evidence.statement: Direct experimental measurement of trastuzumab-HER2 occupancy over time in patients or relevant models to validate the simulated duration above threshold.
In vivo validation of the assumed independent effects of half-life extension and affinity improvement on target occupancy.

simulation_implications.statement: The threefold longer half-life scenario reaches a higher endpoint occupancy than the tenfold stronger affinity scenario.
The threefold longer half-life scenario also accumulates a higher occupancy AUC than the tenfold stronger affinity scenario.
Both intervention scenarios remain above the 90% occupancy threshold at the end of the 180-day observation window, so their time above threshold is censored and cannot be compared for duration.

limitations: Simulated occupancy is a conditional prediction of the stated PK and binding model; it is not evidence of clinical efficacy, safety or an appropriate regimen.
Passages inspected in this investigation did not supply the simulation inputs; the simulation used separately audited reference inputs.
No measured human tumor occupancy, clinical efficacy, or uncertainty prediction.
One-compartment linear PK is a conditional reduction, not a calibrated clinical concentration model.
Target-site exposure is prescribed from central concentration; it is not a measured free tissue concentration.
Binding uses fixed effective sites without depletion, turnover, transport, or avidity.
At least one scenario remains above the analytical occupancy threshold at the horizon; its retention time is censored.
The model is a one-compartment PK with effective reversible target binding and has no measured human tumor occupancy, clinical efficacy, or uncertainty prediction.

next_experiments.proposal: Measure trastuzumab-HER2 occupancy over an extended period in a relevant in vivo model after a single dose.
next_experiments.rationale: This would test whether half-life extension or affinity improvement maintains occupancy above threshold longer beyond the censored simulation window.

next_experiments.proposal: Extend the observation window beyond 180 days for both intervention scenarios to observe when each falls below the 90% threshold.
next_experiments.rationale: The current window cuts off both time-above-threshold curves, preventing a duration comparison.

structural_context.statement: The deposited HER2-HERCEPTIN Fab structure shows drug residues on light chain A and heavy chain B within 4 angstrom of target residues on chain C, including GLY B:103 to LYS C:593 at 2.417 Å, ARG B:50 to ASP C:560 at 2.601 Å, THR A:94 to ASP C:560 at 2.823 Å, HIS A:91 to PRO C:571 at 2.888 Å, and TYR A:92 to LYS C:569 at 2.957 Å.

synthesis.structure_note: Coordinates of 1N8Z show where the binding partners touch in one experimental structure. They cannot determine occupancy over time, half-life, affinity or kinetic rates, so they give context and do not decide this question.

provenance.cutoff_rule: Residue pairs whose closest heavy atoms are within 4 Å (inclusive Euclidean distance) in the first deposited model. Each reported distance is the minimum over that pair's heavy atoms. Hydrogens, waters and glycans are excluded; no symmetry mates or new assemblies are generated.
provenance.scope: Antibody Fab fragment and soluble HER2 extracellular domain; not intact-antibody tissue geometry.
provenance.limitation: Heavy-atom distances in deposited coordinates. They do not establish hydrogen bonds, binding energy, affinity, kinetic rates, mutation effects or clinical outcomes.
